full_judgment:
2. The rule with regard to the cancellation of bail was issued at the instance of and upon an application filed an application filed by the Anti-Corruption Department of the Government of Bangladesh. We have heard the learned Deputy Attorney General in support of the rule and the learned Counsel who appeared for the accused opposite party, perused the petition, the counter affidavit and the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the accused and the records of the case. 

 4. The impugned order granting bail to the accused was passed by the learned Sessions Judge upon an application alleged to have been filed by the accused. While perusing the records of Criminal Misc. Case No. 932 of 1980 of the Sessions Judge's Court out of which the present rule arose, we found that no such application was in fact filed by the, accused. But one application appears to have been filed on his behalf by one Nazma Begum who was reported to be the wife of the accused. We are not in a position to say whether the power was in fact executed by the wire of the accused because in the earlier application for bail filed before the Sessions Judge she was described as Nazma Parvin and not Nazma Begum. Be that as it may, when confronted with this situation on being pointed out by us, the accused in his supplementary affidavit admitted and stated as follows: 

 "Through inadvertence the petitioner omitted in his petition for bail to mention that he did not execute the Vokalatnama filed in Criminal Misc. Case No. 932 of 1980 in the Court of the learned Sessions Judge, Dacca and the same was signed on his behalf by his wife and on this application the learned Sessions Judge was pleased to grant him bail ; and it is apparent there was no application for bail in the eye of law and the order of the learned Sessions Judge granting bail to the petitioner on such application is non-existent in the eye of law and the petitioner cannot lawfully be said to be on bail". 

 6. Before parting with the case we however, deem it necessary in the greater interest of the administration of justice to deal with the facts and circumstances leading to the impugned order in the light of the explanation submitted by the learned sessions Judge as to how and under what circumstances an accused who was taken into custody under orders of this Court was granted bail by him. We have very carefully perused the explanation submitted by the learned Sessions Judge. The bail matter of the accused had, it seems, a chequered career right upto the present stage. This Court had occasion to deal with this matter on an earlier occasion also. The first information report in the instant case was lodged on 27.9.79 alleging various offences under section 161, 165-A, 467, 471/34 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act 11 of 1947. The petitioner surrendered before Mr. A. Khan, the Vacation Judge at Dacca on 17.10.79 and was granted ad interim bail by him. But the bail bond alleged to have been furnished by tile accused haying been found missing, the learned Vacation Judge passed a subsequent order on the same day to the effect that the petitioner be treated on bail after furnishing a valid bail bond. On the same day, a prayer for cancellation of the ad-interim bail was moved before the Vacation Judge who directed the application to be put up after reopening on 22.10.79. 

 "Petitioner surrenders and prays for bail. The learned P. P. Anti-corruption and A.C. prosecution oppose bail on behalf of the State. The case has arisen out of an occurrence which ultimately ended in the murder in broad day-light of a member of this Bar and created considerable sensation. 

 "Charge extremely heinous the alleged illness of wife does not appear to be of any alarming nature Bail prayer rejected Case disposed of. 

 "24.3.80. Heard Case of alleged receiving of illegal gratification. It has arisen out of an occurrence which ultimately ended in the murder in broad day-light of a member of this Bar within the premises of the S.D.O.'s Court. The petitioner surrendered before the Vacation Judge and was granted bail, but some technical defect, having arisen he approached the High Court Division for its correction. On the direction of the Hon'ble Court the petitioner surrendered before this Court on 14.2.80 and was taken into custody. The alleged charge of bribery is yet to be established. The petitioner, therefore, be granted bail subject to the security of Tk. 50,000/- with three sureties of equal amount each, one of the sureties being an Advocate of this Bar and the two others being men of substantial means of Dacca city paying Municipal taxes. 

 11. The matter is indeed serious and if allowed to go unchecked will lead to judicial indiscipline and undermine the confidence of the people in the sanctity and finality of an order passed by a Superior Court. We have on some other occasions also noticed an unfortunate tendency among some of the Judges of the Courts below, to circumvent and by-pass an order passed by this Court. Even if concurrent powers under the law have been given to the Sessions Judge in bail and other matters, they should stay their hands when the matter is in session of the Superior Court. In this particular case, while directing surrender of the accused and to be taken into custody we also had before us his prayer for bail and if we had considered it to be a fit case, we should have granted bail ourselves and not let it to the Sessions Judge to assume jurisdiction which he has now done. If we had wanted this matter to be dealt with by the Sessions Judge on subsequent occasions we would have given explicit directions to that effect and not left the matter for guess or conjecture. The learned Sessions Judge's own order dated 14-2-80 rejecting the prayer for bail and taking the accused into custody under order of this Court clearly slows that he had fully and correctly understood the order and complied with it. as directed leaving no room for any ambiguity in the matter. 

 We have purposely narrated the sequence of events in details only to impress upon and remind all concerned of the oft-quoted legal maxim that justice must not only be done but must also appear to be done. Here is the case of a senior Magistrate charged with serious offences whose alleged corrupt practices led to the broad day-light murder of a young Advocate of the Dacca Bar allegedly by another Advocate of the same Bar. Under the Constitution, all are equal before the law and are entitled to equal treatment under the law, but the entire sequence of events leaves an unfortunate impression that the accused because of his official status was treated deferentially and shown undue indulgence and latitude by allowing him to get away with impunity for all that he had done, Could an accused walk out of the Court after surrender without furnishing bail bond and still be at large without being arrested? In-credible though, this is what had actually happened. Even when the matter was subsequently brought to his notice, the learned Sessions Judge showed utter indifference and passed a most perfunctory order on 22-10-79 quoted above while disposing of the matter as if the Court had nothing further to do. Then, again, bail was granted upon an application filed by someone other than the accused. It is true granting of bail is a matter of discretion vested in the Court but when the discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously without any application of mind it is no exercise of judicial discretion in the eye of law. Courts are the last hope of the people in their hour of need and it is to the Courts that they look for justice against in justice and protection of their rights and liberty. It is, therefore, the sacred duty of the Judges to dispense justice in accordant with law without fear or favour and to conduct themselves in such manner as to inspire confidence of the people in them and through them in the Courts they preside over.
